title: Trace-conditioned assembly edits with one validity correction
hypothesis: Successful expert placement traces let an edit of the recoverable assembly parent seat the nut, once the edit is allowed the pipeline's standard single validity correction (D-025's trace edits failed only on gate_not_a_lever).

prediction.against: summary-only edits of the same parent in the same blocks, also allowed one validity correction, under identical 24-candidate search
prediction.rationale: Same design as R-029 with one correction per edit (the standard allowance) and more demonstration handoffs so that several successful continuations are available.

code_changes: scripts/compare_generation_modes.py (trace-edit-suite: --allow-correction (one validity correction per edit) and --demo-cases)

falsified_by: Zero success in both trace blocks among valid edits, or a fixed-pair interval upper bound below +0.20; an interval containing zero is inconclusive about an advantage. Invalid edits after the correction still score zero (intention to treat).

cost_estimate.breakdown: 10 demo handoffs + 2 blocks x 2 edits x (24 x 5 probe + 30 promotion) = 610; 4 edits + <= 4 corrections

open_question_refs: D-025 (R-029): trace edits untested because of gate_not_a_lever with no correction

approval.note: approved by advisor gpt-6.1-sol (consult call_00052, 'revise' with changes applied) under the user's 2026-10-22 session delegation

controls.note: control is the summary-only edit in the same block with the same correction allowance and search; the metric is already trace minus summary-only

result.notes: Ten learner-to-expert handoffs of the frozen recoverable D-020 parent on demonstration pool 3600: 6/10 successful continuations (gate >= 2 passed); the trace arm saw two of them, every 4th post-handoff step. Two blocks (manifests 3605-3608, search root 3609). Both trace-conditioned edits seat the nut: 1.00 on 30 fresh promotion cases in each block, and they already succeed untrained (step-0 probe 1.0; 10 and 13 of 24 search candidates succeed). Both summary-only edits score 0.00 (probe 0.00, progress stuck at ~0.23 as in D-020..D-024). Trace minus summary-only: +1.000 [1.0, 1.0], 30/0/0 in both blocks. Three of four edits needed their one validation-only correction (both trace edits: gate_not_a_lever-type defects as in D-025), so R-029's no-correction rule is what hid this effect. The winning code reads tcp, obj, goal and gripper through the schema; its numeric constants are centimetre-scale offsets and thresholds, not absolute coordinates. Two blocks share one parent and one demonstration set, so this is a strong but narrow result. 610 episodes, 7 LLM calls.

verdicts.reasoning: Trace-conditioned edits of the recoverable assembly parent score 1.00 on 30 fresh promotion cases in both blocks versus 0.00 for summary-only edits: +1.000 [1.0, 1.0], 30/0/0, far above the predicted +0.20. The effect is the edit itself (step-0 probe success 1.0 before any search), it replicates across two independently generated edit pairs on separate manifests, and the code uses observations rather than copied coordinates. With D-025, the one-correction allowance was what let the traces be tested. Caveat: one parent, one demonstration set, two blocks.
verdicts.next_experiment: Make trace-conditioned editing a pipeline repair step for tasks where the generator plateaus: (1) test it from a different parent or freshly generated structure, (2) on another failing task (e.g. hammer or soccer once scanned), and (3) as a lane in the two-lane search where an expert exists.

verdicts.reasoning: The named summary-only control was measured under the same correction allowance and search budget [logs/next_assembly_traces_s3600/summary.json]. The paired_success_difference was +1.00 with a 95% interval of [1.00, 1.00], exceeding the predicted +0.20 and excluding zero [logs/next_assembly_traces_s3600/summary.json]. Each block achieved trace success of 1.00 versus summary-only success of 0.00 on 30 promotion cases [logs/next_assembly_traces_s3600/summary.json]. All edits were valid after the allowed correction process; both trace edits required correction, but this comparison does not isolate correction's causal contribution [logs/next_assembly_traces_s3600/summary.json]. The result supports the specified comparison narrowly because the blocks shared their parent and demonstration set [logs/next_assembly_traces_s3600/summary.json].
